token_set.name: Hoist the Cup 2025
token_set.description: Hoist the Cup 2025 celebrates the triumphs of the 2025 Stanley Cup champions. This annual Rare collection captures the most electrifying moments from the Florida Panthers journey through the Stanley Cup Playoffs. Relive the thrilling goals, spectacular saves, and defining plays that led to hockey's ultimate glory. Each highlight in this set commemorates the skill, determination, and passion that culminated in hoisting the coveted Stanley Cup.

description:
Joining the Panthers near the trade deadline, Brad Marchand played a pivotal role in securing the team’s second consecutive Stanley Cup championship. Marchand contributed 10 goals, including three game-winners, a stellar +17 plus/minus rating, and 20 points, showcasing his impact on both ends of the ice.  
In Game 5 of the Stanley Cup Final in Edmonton, with the series tied 2-2, Marchand delivered a clutch performance, scoring twice to help the Panthers take control of the series. His first goal came midway through the opening period, displaying his trademark determination and skill. Charging off the faceoff, he won the race to the puck, danced past a defender, and fired a pinpoint shot off the post and in.  
Early in the third period, Marchand struck again. Breaking free for a chance, he slipped past one defender with a slick move, fought off another’s check, and tucked the puck home with precision and grit for his second of the night.  
Marchand’s six goals in the Final, including two game-winners, were instrumental in the Panthers’ triumph over Edmonton and cemented his place as a difference-maker in their championship run.

description:
In Florida’s only series that went the full seven games, defenseman Seth Jones ignited the offense early in the second period, setting the tone for a dominant Panthers performance. Jumping into the rush, Jones carried the puck into the zone, looked off a pass, and rifled a shot far side for his third goal of the postseason.  
Jones was a cornerstone of the Panthers’ success, leading the team in ice time with an average of over 25 minutes per game. His steady presence on the blue line and ability to contribute offensively were pivotal in helping Florida secure their second consecutive Stanley Cup championship.

description:
After clinching the Stanley Cup with his Game 7 heroics the previous season, Sam Reinhart delivered another unforgettable performance for the Florida Panthers, scoring four goals in Game 6 to secure their second consecutive championship.  
Reinhart set the tone early in the first period by forcing a turnover just outside the blue line. Picking up the puck, he drove to the net, made a slick move inside to evade a defender, and fired a shot far side—all while losing his balance and falling to the ice. His opening goal gave the Panthers a lead they never relinquished and marked the start of his four-goal masterpiece.  
Reinhart finished the playoffs tied for second overall in goals (11) and tied for the team lead in points (23), cementing his reputation as a clutch performer on hockey’s biggest stage.

description:
After opening the scoring earlier in the game, defenseman Niko Mikkola delivered another clutch moment in the third period with his second goal of the night. When Carolina dumped the puck into Florida’s zone, Mikkola hustled back to retrieve it, advancing the play up the boards. As the Panthers evaded Carolina’s aggressive forecheck, Mikkola seized the moment, jumping into the rush to create a 3-on-2 advantage.  
Sam Bennett spotted Mikkola streaking down the left side and fed him the puck. Wasting no time, Mikkola ripped a shot top shelf, extending Florida’s lead to two. That goal held as the game-winner in Game 3, putting the Panthers in firm control of the series with a commanding 3-0 lead.

description:
Sergei Bobrovsky, the backbone of Florida’s first Stanley Cup championship last season, was once again a fortress in net for the Panthers in 2025. Known for his consistency, Bobrovsky also delivered clutch saves when his team needed them most.  
In the first round against the Tampa Bay Lightning, he pulled off a stunning sequence of back-to-back saves—kicking out Erik Cernak’s shot with his right pad before denying Gage Goncalves’ rebound attempt with his left arm. Then, in Game 2 of the Stanley Cup Final, Bobrovsky slid across the crease just in time to stone Leon Draisaitl’s one-timer with a pad save. His brilliance continued in Game 3, where, during an early Edmonton power play, he robbed Connor McDavid in the slot with a spectacular pad stop, preserving Florida’s lead—a lead they wouldn’t surrender.  
Bobrovsky’s stellar playoff performance included three shutouts, a .914 save percentage, and a 2.20 goals-against average, solidifying his reputation as one of the league’s premier postseason performers.

description:
Since Matthew Tkachuk joined the Panthers, Florida has made three consecutive Stanley Cup Final appearances, winning the last two. His impact has been undeniable, and it seemed only fitting that he sealed the championship with the clinching goal in Game 6 at home. Late in the first period, Tkachuk, trailing the play, entered the zone and received a perfect pass from Eetu Luostarinen. With the puck, he patiently waited for traffic to form in front of the net before firing a shot past the goaltender. Tkachuk’s postseason heroics were even more remarkable considering he battled through significant injuries, yet still managed to average a point per game and tie for the team lead with 23 points.
